fdroid:com.sleepguard.name: SleepGuard - dead man's switch
fdroid:com.sleepguard.summary: Locks your phone when you fall asleep watching videos. No ads, open source.
fdroid:com.sleepguard.description:
Do you often fall asleep while watching videos or listening to music on your phone? SleepGuard makes sure your device doesn't keep running all night long.
At an interval you choose, a small red circle appears on top of whatever you are watching. Tap it and playback continues as normal. Don't tap it within a few seconds - because you have fallen asleep - and SleepGuard locks the screen, just like pressing the power button. Your video stops and your phone is protected for the rest of the night.
There is also an Audio mode for music, audiobooks and podcasts: instead of a button, SleepGuard works as a simple sleep timer that stops playback after your chosen interval — even with the screen off.
WHY YOU NEED IT
* YouTube and other apps with autoplay: Without SleepGuard, one video starts the next and the next and the next ... until morning. In the worst case the battery is drained empty and your alarm can no longer go off when you need it. SleepGuard stops the chain as soon as you stop responding.
* Netflix, Prime Video and other streaming apps: Fall asleep mid-episode and you wake up not knowing where you dozed off. You waste time scrubbing back to find the spot - sometimes sitting through long ads again and again. SleepGuard locks the screen right when you don't respond, so your streaming app knows where to continue.
HOW IT WORKS
1. Set how often the check button should appear (e.g. every 5 minutes).
2. Set how many seconds you have to react before the screen locks (e.g. 30 seconds).
3. Choose where on the screen the button appears.
4. Start SleepGuard and keep watching.
FEATURES
* Two modes: Video (wake-check button over any app) and Audio (sleep timer for music, audiobooks and podcasts, works also with the screen off)
* Adjustable interval and reaction time
* Eight button positions to choose from
* Reliable timing even in the background (uses the system alarm)
* Completely free, no ads, no tracking, no accounts
PRIVACY
SleepGuard has NO internet permission at all. It cannot send or receive any data. It does exactly two things: show a button and lock the screen. It collects nothing.
PERMISSIONS EXPLAINED
* Display over other apps: to show the red circle on top of your video.
* Device admin (screen lock only): to lock the screen like the power button.
* Foreground service & exact alarm: to make the check button appear on time.
* Ignore battery optimization: so the button still works reliably while another app is in the foreground.
* Notifications (Android 13+): to show the ongoing "SleepGuard is active" notification.
OPEN SOURCE
SleepGuard is free software, licensed under the GNU General Public License v3. The full source code is available so anyone can inspect exactly what the app does: https://github.com/OlafDrechsler/SleepGuard
SUPPORT
SleepGuard is free and will stay free. If it helps you, you can support its developer with a voluntary donation from within the app. There is deliberately no reward in return - it is simply a thank-you.
THE IDEA / THE NAME
The idea for the app comes from a safety system used on trains. In the driver’s cab, there is a button that the driver must press at regular intervals, otherwise the train will automatically stop. By pressing the button, the driver confirms that he or she is awake. Colloquially, this button is called a “dead man’s switch,” and so the app is also called “SleepGuard – dead man’s switch.”

firefox-addons:2727714.description:
GitHub Privacy redacts dates on GitHub. You can choose the level of redaction.
Data privacy and protection has become a big issue nowadays. Not everyone is confident in sharing their data and not every data shown is necessary for others.

firefox-addons:2858328.name: Site Timer Productivity Helper
firefox-addons:2858328.summary: A simple extension which allows for soft blacklisting sites to limit time wasting or, "doom scrolling." It supports blacklisting entire domains, or simply paths of domains. Customizable timers and lightweight. Simple in scope and privacy friendly.
firefox-addons:2858328.description:
A simple extension which allows a user to input either domains (eg: reddit.com ) or specific paths of domains (eg: youtube.com/shorts ) to apply a time limiting functionality against for active tab usage. It's similar to a Pomodoro Timer, but targeting specific websites, even exclusively specific paths for websites. 
Users specify a time limit in seconds which applies to all blacklisted sites (timer carries over between blacklisted sites - so if visiting two different blacklisted sites back to back, the timer does not start to count down/reset and counts both sites under a single blacklisted timer). Users also specify a reset timer which will only count when visiting non-blacklisted sites. When the reset timer expires, the main blacklisted site timer will reset. 
After the blacklisted/domain timer expires, a popup page telling the user to do something else will appear. This behavior will continue until the reset timer expires, via spending time on non-blacklisted sites. 
 IMPORTANT: Settings changed in the extension preferences page will not take effect until the extension restarts! Read below for more information! 
 Readme / How to use: 
Users install extension -> visit "about:addons" aka the manage extensions page -> click three dots for Site Timer Productivity Helper -> Preferences
Then, users can add blacklisted sites in the top field. The timer value for blacklisted domains, and the reset timer can also be set below. Finally, there is a button to restart the extension, and a list of currently blacklisted sites. 
IMPORTANT: The< "restart extension" button is there for a good reason - the settings changed in the preferences page do not take effect unless the extension is restarted. The timers and domains will update on the page in real time after settings changes to reflect what the extension is storing in local storage for extension settings, but the live behavior of the app will not care about these changes until the extension restarts. Therefore, click the extension restart button after any changes are made to the domain blacklist, or timer values. 
 So does this mean... (use cases and functionality clarification) 
I made this addon because I wanted to blacklist specific sites for extended usage, without impacting the entire domain. For example, I want to make it easy to kick myself off of extended YouTube Shorts sessions, without stopping me from using YouTube for standard videos. 
During use, the extension will compare the root domain (eg: youtube.com ) against the blacklist. If no exact match is found within the domain blacklist, it then begins to consider the user's current tab's path, from the top path down to the end. If any match is found, it'll blacklist the site. So you can be on, " example.com/path1/path2/path3 " and if the blacklist has an entry of, " example.com/path1 " it'll still blacklist, " example.com/..../path3 ". However, if you blacklisted ".../path3" without other entries for this domain and were visiting only ".../path1" then it would not blacklist the page. 
It treats all matches between blacklisted sites as equal. Swapping from one blacklisted site to another doesn't change the timer status, and currently I don't have anything set up to change the timer for a specific site. 
If the user uses up a portion of the blacklist timer BUT DOES NOT EXPIRE IT, then the user goes back to non-blacklisted sites, the blacklist timer will slowly start to tick down back to zero.

apple-macos:6758882595.name: T-Rex VPN - Secure VPN Client
apple-macos:6758882595.description:
T-REX VPN is a privacy-focused VPN client that routes your internet traffic through an encrypted tunnel, keeping your data safe on public Wi-Fi and untrusted networks.
KEY FEATURES:
1. Server Scanner
Test all available VPN servers directly from the app. The scanner checks each location for availability and measures latency, so you can pick the fastest server before connecting.
2. Location Selection
Browse VPN servers organized by country and city. Select a specific location or let the app automatically choose the best available server. Save your preferred locations to Favorites for quick access.
3. Connection Reliability
Built-in connection verification confirms your traffic is routed through the VPN after each connect. If a server becomes unreachable, auto-reconnect seamlessly switches to another available server. Continuous ping monitoring detects connection issues early and triggers recovery automatically.
4. Network Statistics
View real-time download and upload speeds, latency, and total data transferred while connected.
5. Privacy & Security
All traffic is encrypted using industry-standard protocols (TLS 1.3, AES-256-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305). The app uses a TUN interface to create a system-wide VPN tunnel via Apple's Network Extension framework.
6. Subscription Plans
Choose from Basic, Premium, or Family plans with monthly or yearly billing. Subscribe directly through the App Store with in-app purchase.
7. Account & Devices
Create an account with email or sign in with Apple. View and manage all your connected devices from within the app.
8. Localization
Available in 21 languages including English, Chinese, Spanish, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Arabic, Russian, Portuguese, and more.
